content.text:
The report is valid and reproducible on current `main`. This is a genuine O(n) process-spawning performance bug, not a Git maintenance problem or a corrupt repository.

I reproduced the reporter’s exact process counts with the current `2026.9.3-DEBUG` checkout:

| Checkpoints | First rebuild | Second rebuild |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 336 Git processes / 1.85s | 336 / 2.08s |
| 24 | 992 / 8.67s | 992 / 10.12s |

The linear formula is exactly `41 × checkpoints + 8`, predicting 3,288 processes for the discussion’s 80-checkpoint fixture. Existing metadata caches provide no improvement on the second rebuild.

The cause is confirmed:

- A synchronized head change triggers rebuilding under the history lock in [checkpoint.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/da3d/mise/src/system/history/checkpoint.rs:222).
- `checkpoint_refs()` fully parses every commit merely to obtain an ID, although the ID is the commit hash: [shadow.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/da3d/mise/src/system/history/shadow.rs:547).
- The rebuild scans every commit for annotations twice, then parses every ordinary checkpoint again: [checkpoint.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/da3d/mise/src/system/history/checkpoint.rs:749).
- `read_meta()` invokes multiple Git subprocesses and even reads the tree twice: [shadow.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/da3d/mise/src/system/history/shadow.rs:560).
- Although metadata is cached, rebuilding only writes the cache; it never reads it: [store.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/da3d/mise/src/system/history/store.rs:748).

The proposed solution is directionally correct:

1. Take checkpoint identities directly from commit IDs.
2. Batch-read annotation metadata.
3. Cache the unannotated, commit-derived record and validate it against the exact commit and relevant schema/path/profile context.
4. Reapply annotations from current ancestry on every rebuild, preventing removed annotations from surviving a reset.

This preserves Git as the source of truth while reducing a warm rebuild to effectively constant Git-process overhead. The thousands of processes are sequential rather than a concurrent fork bomb, but holding the history lock throughout makes the user-visible delay severe.

I found no existing fix in repository history, and the relevant code remains unchanged on current `main`. My recommendation is to treat [Discussion #12993](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12993) as a confirmed performance bug and invite or implement the prototype as a PR with the reported process-count regression test. No source changes were made during this investigation.

Yes—for `history_messages()` in this PR, not for the entire history backend.
